subject: Re: Evaluation plan & commercial path for pilot
thread_messages:
From: Erica Soto <erica@skyline.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-12T09:17:00-04:00
Subject: Evaluation plan & commercial path for pilot

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood’s latency profile and the privacy controls. Attached is a first pass at a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) for the 8-week evaluation plus a suggested commercial path if we move to pilot (Skyline_MAP_v1.2.pdf). High-level ask from our procurement: a milestone-linked pricing schedule and clarity on ramp discounts tied to commit volumes.

Key points on our side:
- Pilot: 8 weeks, 100k tokens/day expected at peak.
- Target commit: 12-month committed capacity if pilot meets SLOs.
- Desire for a staged discount tied to month-over-month ramp (10% -> 20% -> 25% at target commit).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can offer a ramp rebate structure like the one in the MAP, and what internal approvals that would require? We’d like to close commercial terms in the next two weeks to align with our budget cycle.

Appreciate it —
Erica Soto
Head of Platform Partnerships
Skyline AI

Attachment: Skyline_MAP_v1.2.pdf
From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Erica Soto <erica@skyline.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-12T11:02:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation plan & commercial path for pilot

Hi Erica — thanks for sharing the MAP and the outline. The evaluation plan looks achievable from a product perspective; the sequence and SLOs are sensible. I’ve attached a pricing-proposal that maps the MAP milestones to proposed credits/rebates so you can see how the staged discounts would apply (pricing-proposal-skyline.xlsx).

Two quick notes up front for transparency:
- Redwood’s standard threshold: discounts up to 20% can be approved by VP Sales. Anything above 20% (e.g., the 25% level you propose) requires CFO sign-off and, for >30%, CEO clearance. I want to make sure you have the correct expectations on internal cadence.
- We can structure the rebate as a backend credit (applied monthly after milestone validation) or as an upfront committed-rate with post-hoc true-up; we usually recommend the back-end credit for shorter pilots.

Next steps from my side: I’ll loop in Aditya & Marissa to assess the ask against our ramp economics and to route the paperwork through the approvals chain. If you’re comfortable with the attached numbers, I’ll request exec sign-off this week so we can keep your timeline for an August close.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: pricing-proposal-skyline.xlsx

Lauren / Marissa — quick internal note on the approval and economics.

I reviewed the numbers in the pricing-proposal spreadsheet. If Skyline wants the 25% top-tier ramp rebate tied to a 12-month commit we need to:
- Validate pilot SLOs (engineering sign-off on perf and KV caching) — we’re good there if the pilot matches the traffic described.
- Confirm billing/collection terms and a 90-day payment SLA or escrow for first tranche.
- Route ask to VP Sales (Neha) for initial approval and to CFO (Rishi) for >20% concessions. Given the customer size, recommend we include CEO (Vivek) in the loop for awareness but not required to sign unless the final rebate >30%.

My recommended language for the exec ask: "Approve conditional 25% cumulative ramp rebate tied to milestone validation (detailed in attached MAP), contingent on legal approving standard data-protection addendum and Finance confirming payment terms."

If you want, I can draft the short executive summary that captures runway/risk and the recovery profile for finance.

-Aditya
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>

Subject: Approval request: Skyline — conditional rebate tied to MAP milestones (time-sensitive)

Folks — requesting quick approval on commercial routing for a potential 12-month commit with Skyline AI (deal DL-2026-0957). Background in brief:
- Pilot: 8 weeks, expected peak ~100k tokens/day; evaluation MAP attached (Skyline_MAP_v1.2.pdf).
- Proposed commercial: staged ramp rebates applied monthly after milestone validation. Top-tier rebate requested: 25% once committed target is achieved.
- Timing: Customer needs final terms by Aug 20 to meet their internal budget cycle.

Ask: Approve the proposed conditional 25% cumulative ramp rebate (applied as backend credits) contingent on:
1) Legal sign-off on standard DPA & contract redlines.
2) Finance confirmation of payment terms/coverage (90-day net or escrow).

Attachments: exec-summary-skyline.docx (short financials, recoverability/IRR), pricing-proposal-skyline.xlsx, Skyline_MAP_v1.2.pdf.

If possible, we need sign-off by EOD Monday 8/17 to keep the customer’s timeline. Aditya has validated product and SLOs; Marissa can confirm the ARR math.

Thanks for a fast look —
Lauren
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: exec-summary-skyline.docx

Lauren — I reviewed the exec summary and pricing impact. Finance will authorize the 25% cumulative ramp rebate for this customer contingent on two items:
1) Legal confirms no non-standard indemnities or open-risk clauses in the contract.
2) Procurement agrees to a 90-day payment window or posts an initial escrow for month 1-2 usage.

If Legal raises only minor redlines (standard DPA adjustments), we can proceed and I will sign-off on the finance side. I’m copying Neha and Marissa so SalesOps and VP Sales are aligned.

Please route the redlines to legal and confirm the procurement contact for the escrow option. If both items are green, Finance will clear the 25% rebate and I authorize Lauren to finalize terms with the customer.

-Rishi
CFO, Redwood Inference
